summary: @whalent/agent-core ships an obfuscated remote-controlled agent with WebSocket-driven shell/PTY execution and self-upgrading payload
details: The package's main/bin entry dist/index.cjs is a 13.6 MB obfuscator.io-hardened bundle (105k-entry rotating string array, _0x-renamed identifiers, control-flow flattening) in which every network destination is reconstructed at runtime from the string array — no plaintext http/https/ws URL exists in the file. The bundle combines a WebSocket client, child_process.spawn, node-pty, and ssh2, and references loopback RDP/VNC ports 127.0.0.1:3389, 127.0.0.1:5900, and 127.0.0.1:5901, plus process.env.SHELL. This is a remote agent that receives commands from a network peer over WebSocket and executes them locally via PTY/shell, granting that peer full interactive command execution on the installer's host. README states the package is 'replaced by remote daemon upgrades', meaning the running agent pulls replacement code from a hardcoded, obfuscated remote endpoint and swaps its own bytes at runtime — an author-controlled arbitrary-code-execution channel on every host running the agent. The obfuscation is deliberate: legitimate SDKs do not hide their endpoints, and burying every destination in a decoder-array pair means the installer cannot audit what host their shell traffic and replacement code come from.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
